context: Current closing price of RTX Corp (RTX): $193.44 USD as of 2026-11-19.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift assumption from what appears to be a baseline price near $193–194. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $193.8 essentially implies near-flat movement, which is typical when there is no strong directional catalyst immediately visible — short-term price action tends to mean-revert or drift only slightly, so I anchored close to the prevailing level. At the one-week horizon, the slight uptick to $194.5 reflects a small positive drift assumption, consistent with the historical tendency of equity or asset prices to trend mildly upward over short periods in the absence of negative shocks. At the one-month horizon, $196.0 extends that drift further, incorporating a modest expected return over roughly 20 trading days while acknowledging that the compounding effect of daily uncertainty begins to accumulate meaningfully.

The confidence interval widths were primarily driven by realized and implied volatility assumptions at each horizon. At one day, the interval is relatively tight ($189.5–$198.1, roughly ±2.2%), reflecting that intraday and overnight price swings are constrained compared to longer windows. At one week, the interval widens to approximately ±4.4% around the point estimate, capturing the increased probability of a macro data release, earnings surprise, or sentiment shift materially moving the price. At one month, the interval stretches to roughly ±8.7%, reflecting the full accumulation of daily uncertainty and the heightened chance of a regime-changing event within a 30-day window.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a surprisingly strong earnings report, an unexpected Federal Reserve pivot toward easier monetary policy, or a broad risk-on sentiment surge could push prices well above $213 at the one-month horizon. On the downside, a significant deterioration in macroeconomic data, an escalation in geopolitical tensions, a credit event in a systemically important institution, or a sudden liquidity crunch could easily breach the $179 lower bound. Tail risks are always fatter than a simple symmetric distribution implies, so the actual probability of extreme outcomes is somewhat higher than the 10% I nominally assigned to the tails.

It is also worth noting that my intervals assume relatively stable market microstructure and liquidity conditions. In periods of stress, bid-ask spreads widen, correlations spike, and price discovery becomes noisier — all of which would argue for even wider intervals than stated. The one-month forecast in particular carries the most model uncertainty, as it depends heavily on assumptions about drift and volatility that may shift materially if the broader macro environment changes character during that window.
